questions.q: What does an 85% code coverage number actually tell you?
options: 85% of the tests in the suite passed
85% of lines (or branches) of code ran at least once during the test run
The code is 85% free of bugs
85% of the team's pull requests included tests
questions.explain: Coverage measures how much of the source code was executed during testing — it says nothing directly about test pass rate or bug count.

questions.q: Why is a high coverage number not a guarantee of correctness?
options: Coverage tools frequently miscalculate percentages
A test can execute a function without asserting anything meaningful about its behavior, and still count as 'covering' it
Coverage only applies to JavaScript projects
High coverage always means the code has fewer lines
questions.explain: Coverage tracks what code ran, not whether the test actually verified correct behavior — a weak or empty assertion still counts as coverage.

questions.q: What does `--cov-fail-under=80` do in a pytest command?
options: Limits the test suite to 80 tests
Fails the step if total coverage drops below 80%, acting as a built-in quality gate
Skips any test that takes longer than 80 seconds
Sets the coverage report's file size limit to 80KB
questions.explain: This flag is the quality gate itself — it fails the command's exit code (and therefore the pipeline step) once coverage falls under the given threshold.

questions.q: Why is diff coverage (patch coverage) often more useful day to day than overall project coverage?
options: Diff coverage is always a higher percentage
It measures only the lines changed in a specific pull request, letting a gate require new code to be well-tested without demanding old code be retroactively tested
Overall coverage cannot be measured accurately
Diff coverage replaces the need for a test suite entirely
questions.explain: A large legacy codebase may never reach a high overall percentage, but requiring high diff coverage stops new, untested code from being added going forward.

questions.q: What three elements does every quality gate — coverage or otherwise — share?
options: A screenshot, a caption, and a reviewer
A measurement, a threshold, and a pipeline step that fails the build when the threshold is crossed
A Dockerfile, a registry, and a tag
A branch, a commit, and a pull request
questions.explain: Whether it's coverage, static-analysis findings, or test pass rate, a quality gate always consists of measuring something, defining a threshold, and failing the build when that threshold is crossed.
